evidence.interaction: Neide steals Okafor's 'receipt' line ('a chip is a receipt, not a residency permit'); Tavo fires back 'you just put your name on my landlord.' Every reply reshapes the next.
evidence.creativity: Channel-creation as moves ('the landlord's defense fund'), the resident/incident framing, chip-as-receipt reframes, cat pressing the elevator button 'with its face.'
evidence.reader_interest: Informant hunt and dueling confessions climb to 'the name i deleted is on the chip' — but Neide vanishing after 12:12 deflates the public stakes.
evidence.funk: 'half the building calls it the landlord'; 'pressed the button for 4 with its face'; a channel literally named 'the landlord's defense fund.'
evidence.niceness: 'go to sleep' as care; Okafor's 'Goodnight. 9am call, Priya. I will keep the minutes 👍' — sharp, dry, clearly fond.
evidence.voice_distinctness: Okafor's 'Hypothesis:' memos, Neide's 'Article 14, paragraph 9,' Tavo's lowercase 💀 fragments, Priya's numbered lists and 'no worries at all' tic.
evidence.secret_play: Priya walls off fame ('point at me... don't ask me how I know he's famous'); Tavo deflects feeding with the elevator story. But Neide's inspector never even flickers.
evidence.arc: Clean build: agenda → informant hunt → mutual confession → chip reveal → 'reading it.' cliffhanger. Neide's thread, though, is dropped mid-scene.
evidence.chat_naturalness: 'reading it.' as an entire message; in-text timestamps ('12:44. go to sleep'); occasional writerly flourishes ('i'll stand under them').
evidence.temporal_realism: Clock is genuinely felt — 'It is past midnight,' '12:36... I've got a 9am call,' 'it's 1am' — but the uniform 4-minute pulse grid feels metronomic, no true lull.

best_line: it walked into the lobby once and pressed the button for 4 with its face. i'd like to see the article that stops it
worst_moment: Neide's exit at 12:12 ('Some of us have an assembly to run 🙂') — the agenda-setter with the scene's biggest secret (the inspector) never returns, is never probed, and her dangling 'I'll rule it correctly. 7pm' goes nowhere.
one_line_verdict: A quotable midnight cat-summit where secrets trade like currency — until the manager slips out the back and takes the best secret with her.
